title: Dhul Hijjah: the best days
hookLine: extra deeds in the first ten
tomorrow: the pilgrims stand on a plain. what about everyone at home?

lines: A WEEK WITH NO SPARE INCH.
NO DAYS BETTER FOR GOOD DEEDS.
cards: Exams on Monday. A double shift on Wednesday. A cousin's move on the weekend.

Some weeks have no spare inch in them, and the last thing anyone wants is a list of extra things to do. Then the calendar turns to Dhul Hijjah, the month of the Hajj, and its first ten days arrive with a claim attached.
The Prophet ﷺ said that no good deeds done on other days are better than those done in these days. His companions were so surprised they asked him a question back.

teach.b: Ibn 'Abbas tells it, in Sahih al-Bukhari. The companions asked: not even jihad, striving in God's path? And he said: not even jihad, except a man who goes out with his life and his wealth and comes back with none of it.
So ordinary deeds in these ten days carry a weight the companions didn't expect.
Some commentators hear these days in the Qur'an too, where God swears by the dawn, and, in Pickthall's words, "And ten nights." The pilgrims are in Mecca. But the hadith isn't only about them.
It's about anyone, anywhere, doing good in these days.

People keep it in small ways: a voluntary fast, the takbir said out loud, God is greater, in the market and at home, a little extra charity, a page more of Qur'an. Here's the part that fits a crammed week.
Nothing in the hadith asks for something heroic. It asks for good deeds, the regular kind, done in a season when they count for more. A short dhikr between study blocks.
A call to a grandparent on the drive.
A few coins in a jar. The ten days don't need an empty calendar. They need small things, more of them.

how: In the first ten days of Dhul Hijjah many Muslims add voluntary fasts, say the takbir aloud, give extra charity and read more Qur'an, while the pilgrims gather in Mecca for the Hajj.

games.q: what goes with what — tap the pairs.
p: no days better for good deeds

s: the hadith on the ten days is only for pilgrims at Hajj
it's about good deeds in these days, by anyone, anywhere.
the companions asked: not even jihad?
and he said not even that, except one who goes out with life and wealth and comes back with none of it.

games.q: your neighbor is home sick through the first ten days of Dhul Hijjah and feels she's missing them. what fits?
o: she's sick, so the ten days just don't apply to her this year.
small deeds from bed still count: dhikr, a kind call, a little charity.
she should push through and fast anyway, so the reward isn't lost.
games.why: the hadith asks for good deeds, not heroics. the regular kind, done in these days, carry extra weight, even from a sickbed.

practice: On paper, write the numbers one to ten down the side. Next to each, one small extra thing that would fit that day: a coin given, a call to an elder, a short fast, a page.
Keep the list in front of you and look it over for the rest of the sit.

wordCard.voice: Dhul Hijjah: the month of the Hajj. Its first ten days, the Prophet said, have no equal for good deeds.

orig.note: Arabic: the month of the Hajj, whose first ten days are honored for good deeds.

carryVoice: The line for today: the best ten, ordinary deeds in a stretch that weighs them more. Small things, done more.
